questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The point group of staggered ferrocene, $[\text{Fe}(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)_2]$, is
questions.explanationEn: Staggered ferrocene has a principal $C_5$ axis passing through the centers of both cyclopentadienyl rings, five perpendicular $C_2$ axes passing through Fe, five dihedral mirror planes ($\sigma_d$) bisecting the $C_2$ axes, an inversion center $i$, and an $S_{10}$ axis, but no $\sigma_h$. These elements define the $D_{5d}$ point group (whereas eclipsed ferrocene is $D_{5h}$). Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following point groups allows a molecule to possess a permanent electric dipole moment?
questions.explanationEn: A molecule can have a permanent electric dipole moment only if its point group is $C_1$, $C_s$, $C_n$, or $C_{nv}$ (where at least one Cartesian coordinate transforms as the totally symmetric representation). Point groups with an inversion center ($D_{2h}, C_{2h}$) or multiple high-order axes ($T_d$) force $\mu = 0$. In $C_{3v}$, the dipole lies along the $C_3$ axis. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of fundamental vibrational modes for a linear triatomic molecule such as $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ is
questions.explanationEn: A linear polyatomic molecule containing $N$ atoms has $3N - 5$ vibrational degrees of freedom (3 translational + 2 rotational). For triatomic linear $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ ($N = 3$), the number of vibrational modes is $3(3) - 5 = 4$ (symmetric stretch, asymmetric stretch, and a doubly degenerate bend). Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a Jablonski diagram, radiative relaxation from the lowest triplet excited state ($T_1$) to the singlet ground state ($S_0$) is called
questions.explanationEn: Phosphorescence is the radiative emission of a photon accompanying the spin-forbidden transition $T_1 \to S_0$ ($\Delta S \neq 0$), which leads to long lifetimes ($10^{-3}$ to $10^1\text{ s}$). Fluorescence is $S_1 \to S_0$ (spin-allowed), whereas internal conversion and intersystem crossing are non-radiative processes. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an organic radical with $g = 2.0023$, the EPR resonance condition $h\nu = g\mu_B B_0$ implies that at a higher microwave frequency $\nu$ (e.g., Q-band vs X-band), the resonance magnetic field $B_0$
questions.explanationEn: From the fundamental EPR resonance condition $B_0 = \frac{h\nu}{g\mu_B}$, for a fixed $g$-factor, the required magnetic field $B_0$ is directly proportional to the microwave operating frequency $\nu$ (e.g., $\sim 0.34\text{ T}$ at X-band $9.5\text{ GHz}$ vs $\sim 1.25\text{ T}$ at Q-band $35\text{ GHz}$). Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following molecules belong to the $D_{3h}$ point group?
questions.explanationEn: Trigonal bipyramidal $\text{PF}_5$ (D), trigonal planar $\text{SO}_3$ (B), and eclipsed ethane (C) all possess a $C_3$ axis, three perpendicular $C_2$ axes, and a horizontal mirror plane $\sigma_h$, placing them in $D_{3h}$. Staggered ethane (A) lacks $\sigma_h$ and belongs to $D_{3d}$. Hence, (B), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following nuclei have a nuclear spin quantum number $I = \frac{1}{2}$?
questions.explanationEn: The nuclei $^{13}\text{C}$, $^{19}\text{F}$, and $^{31}\text{P}$ all have nuclear spin $I = \frac{1}{2}$ (making them ideal, sharp-line spin-$1/2$ NMR nuclei). By contrast, $^{14}\text{N}$ (7 protons, 7 neutrons) has nuclear spin $I = 1$ (quadrupolar). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of symmetry operations (order $h$) in the point group of benzene ($D_{6h}$) is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For any $D_{nh}$ point group, the order is $h = 4n$. For benzene ($D_{6h}$, $n = 6$), $h = 4 \times 6 = 24$ (comprising $E, 2C_6, 2C_3, C_2, 3C_2', 3C_2'', i, 2S_3, 2S_6, \sigma_h, 3\sigma_d, 3\sigma_v$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a rigid linear molecule with rotational constant $\tilde{B} = 2.00\text{ cm}^{-1}$, the wavenumber separation between two consecutive Stokes lines in its pure rotational Raman spectrum is _____ $\text{cm}^{-1}$ (rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.explanationEn: In pure rotational Raman spectroscopy ($\Delta J = +2$), the Stokes lines appear at shifts $\tilde{\nu}_J = \tilde{\nu}_0 - \tilde{B}(4J + 6)$. Thus, the spacing between consecutive Stokes lines ($J$ and $J + 1$) is $4\tilde{B} = 4 \times 2.00 = 8.0\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of hyperfine lines arising solely from coupling of the unpaired electron to a single $^{14}\text{N}$ nucleus ($I = 1$) in the EPR spectrum of a nitroxide radical (such as TEMPO) is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For an unpaired electron coupled to a single $^{14}\text{N}$ nucleus ($n = 1, I = 1$), the number of hyperfine lines is $2nI + 1 = 2(1)(1) + 1 = 3$ lines of equal intensity ($1:1:1$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the $C_{3v}$ point group (classes $E, 2C_3, 3\sigma_v$; characters: $A_1: 1, 1, 1$; $A_2: 1, 1, -1$; $E: 2, -1, 0$), a reducible representation has characters $\Gamma = (6, 0, 2)$. Its decomposition into irreducible representations is

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a tetrahedral molecule $\text{CH}_4$ ($T_d$ point group). The $3N = 15$ Cartesian displacement vectors on the five atoms generate a reducible representation $\Gamma_{3N}$ whose character under the $C_3$ operation is
questions.explanationEn: Under a $C_3$ rotation of $\text{CH}_4$ (passing through C and one H atom), $n_{\text{unshifted}} = 2$ atoms remain unshifted (the central C and the axial H). The contribution per unshifted atom to the trace of the $3 \times 3$ rotation matrix for angle $\theta = 120^\circ$ is $1 + 2\cos(120^\circ) = 1 + 2(-\frac{1}{2}) = 0$. Therefore, $\chi_{3N}(C_3) = 2 \times 0 = 0$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the $^{19}\text{F}$ NMR spectrum of $\text{SF}_4$ recorded at $-90\,^\circ\text{C}$ (slow-exchange limit, seesaw $C_{2v}$ geometry), the spectrum consists of
optionsEn: a doublet and a quartet in a $3:1$ ratio
questions.explanationEn: Seesaw $\text{SF}_4$ ($C_{2v}$) has two equivalent axial fluorines ($\text{F}_a$) and two equivalent equatorial fluorines ($\text{F}_e$). At $-90\,^\circ\text{C}$, pseudorotation is frozen; the two $\text{F}_a$ nuclei split the $\text{F}_e$ resonance into a triplet ($n+1=3$), and the two $\text{F}_e$ nuclei split the $\text{F}_a$ resonance into a triplet, producing two triplets of equal ($2:2 = 1:1$) integrated intensity. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the isotropic EPR spectrum of the bis(salicylaldiminato)copper(II) complex ($\text{Cu}$ has $^{63/65}\text{Cu}$, $I = \frac{3}{2}$, and the two equivalent coordinated $^{14}\text{N}$ donor atoms each have $I = 1$), the total number of hyperfine and superhyperfine lines (neglecting ligand $^1\text{H}$ coupling) is
questions.explanationEn: The single unpaired electron on $\text{Cu(II)}$ ($d^9, S = 1/2$) couples to the $^{63/65}\text{Cu}$ nucleus ($I = 3/2$), giving $2(1)(3/2) + 1 = 4$ hyperfine lines. Each of these $4$ lines is further split by superhyperfine coupling to $2$ equivalent $^{14}\text{N}$ nuclei ($I = 1$) into $2(2)(1) + 1 = 5$ lines. Total lines $= 4 \times 5 = 20$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following molecules are CHIRAL (optically active, lacking all improper rotation axes $S_n$ including $\sigma$ and $i$)?
questions.explanationEn: A molecule is chiral if and only if its point group contains no improper rotation axis $S_n$ (which includes $\sigma = S_1$ and $i = S_2$). Skew $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ ($C_2$, B), $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$ ($D_3$, A), and *trans*-$1,2$-dimethylcyclopropane ($C_2$, C) possess only proper rotation axes and are chiral. Methane ($T_d$, D) has $6\sigma_d$ and $6S_4$ elements and is achiral. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about electronic selection rules and spectra of diatomic molecules are CORRECT?
optionsEn: The orbital angular momentum projection selection rule is $\Delta \Lambda = 0, \pm 1$.
The spin selection rule is $\Delta S = 0$.
For homonuclear diatomics, the Laporte parity rule allows $g \leftrightarrow u$ and forbids $g \leftrightarrow g$ and $u \leftrightarrow u$.
questions.explanationEn: Electric-dipole selection rules for diatomic molecules are $\Delta S = 0$ (B), $\Delta\Lambda = 0, \pm 1$ (A), $+ \leftrightarrow +$ / $- \leftrightarrow -$ for $\Sigma \to \Sigma$, and Laporte parity $g \leftrightarrow u$ (D). Statement (C) violates both the Laporte rule ($g \not\to g$) and the $\Sigma$ reflection rule ($+ \not\to -$). Hence, (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about the Beer-Lambert law ($A = \varepsilon c l$) and photophysical kinetics are CORRECT?
optionsEn: The fluorescence quantum yield is given by $\Phi_f = \frac{k_f}{k_f + k_{\text{ic}} + k_{\text{isc}}}$.
Apparent deviations from the Beer-Lambert law can occur at high concentrations or when the absorbing species undergoes concentration-dependent dimerization.
Doubling the path length $l$ doubles the molar absorption coefficient $\varepsilon$.
questions.explanationEn: From $A = -\log_{10}(T)$, $T = 0.10 \implies A = 1.0$ (B). High concentrations (intermolecular interactions, refractive index changes) and chemical equilibria such as dimerization cause deviations from linearity (C). The fluorescence quantum yield is the fraction of excited $S_1$ molecules decaying radiatively: $\Phi_f = \frac{k_f}{k_f + k_{\text{ic}} + k_{\text{isc}}}$ (A). Statement (D) is false because $\varepsilon$ is an intensive molecular property independent of $l$. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The fundamental ($v = 0 \to 1$) and first overtone ($v = 0 \to 2$) IR absorption bands of a diatomic molecule appear at $2886\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and $5668\text{ cm}^{-1}$, respectively. The anharmonicity constant $x_e$ (rounded off to four decimal places) is _____.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Group Theory & Molecular Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an organic chromophore in its $S_1$ state, the first-order rate constants for fluorescence, internal conversion, and intersystem crossing are $k_f = 4.0 \times 10^7\text{ s}^{-1}$, $k_{\text{ic}} = 2.5 \times 10^7\text{ s}^{-1}$, and $k_{\text{isc}} = 1.5 \times 10^7\text{ s}^{-1}$, respectively. The observed fluorescence lifetime $\tau_f$ (in $\text{ns}$, rounded off to one decimal place) is _____.
questions.explanationEn: The observed lifetime of the $S_1$ state is the reciprocal of the sum of all first-order decay rate constants: $\tau_f = \frac{1}{k_f + k_{\text{ic}} + k_{\text{isc}}} = \frac{1}{(4.0 + 2.5 + 1.5) \times 10^7\text{ s}^{-1}} = \frac{1}{8.0 \times 10^7}\text{ s} = 1.25 \times 10^{-8}\text{ s} = 12.5\text{ ns}$.
